questions.question: What does Amazon Web Services (AWS) Enterprise Support offer? (Select TWO)

options.text: A response time of less than 15 minutes for all issues

explanation.summary: The 15-minute response time applies only to business-critical system down cases, not all issues, making this statement an overgeneralization of Enterprise Support SLAs.
explanation.why: AWS Enterprise Support provides tiered response times based on case severity, not a blanket 15-minute response for all issues. The service level agreements specify different response times for different severity levels: critical business-critical system down cases receive less than 15-minute response times, urgent production system impaired cases receive less than 1-hour response, important production system down cases receive less than 4-hour response, and normal guidance cases receive less than 24-hour response. The 15-minute SLA represents AWS's fastest response commitment reserved for the most critical situations where entire business operations are affected. Applying this response time to all issues would be operationally impractical and unnecessary, as not all customer inquiries require emergency response. Lower severity issues like general guidance questions, feature requests, or non-urgent technical questions receive appropriate but less immediate response times. Understanding the tiered SLA structure helps customers set appropriate expectations and correctly classify case severity to receive appropriate response times. The statement all issues incorrectly suggests every support case regardless of severity receives 15-minute response, which would misrepresent the actual Enterprise Support offering.

options.text: A dedicated AWS technical account manager (TAM)

explanation.summary: AWS Enterprise Support includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager who serves as the customer's primary point of contact, providing proactive guidance, architectural reviews, operational support, and advocacy within AWS to help customers achieve their business objectives.
keyPoints: TAM serves as single point of contact and trusted advisor for Enterprise Support customers
Provides proactive guidance on AWS best practices, architecture, and optimization
Conducts regular account reviews, workload reviews, and operational health assessments
Coordinates with AWS service teams and support engineers for complex technical issues
Helps customers prepare for events like product launches, migrations, or peak traffic periods
Develops relationships with customer technical teams understanding business context and goals
Available during business hours in customer's region with escalation paths for urgent needs
examples: TAM conducts quarterly business reviews analyzing AWS usage, identifying optimization opportunities, and planning future initiatives
Before major product launch, TAM coordinates preparation including load testing, architecture review, and support escalation procedures
TAM facilitates Well-Architected Framework review identifying security, reliability, and performance improvements
During migration project, TAM provides guidance on migration strategies, connects customer with specialist teams, and monitors progress
TAM helps customer navigate AWS services recommending appropriate solutions for specific business requirements
After identifying cost optimization opportunities, TAM works with customer to implement Reserved Instance strategy saving 40% on compute costs
explanation.additionalInfo: The Technical Account Manager represents one of the most valuable and distinctive features of AWS Enterprise Support, providing personalized, proactive guidance that goes far beyond reactive troubleshooting available in lower support tiers. Unlike Basic, Developer, or Business Support where customers interact with different support engineers for each case, Enterprise Support customers receive a dedicated TAM who develops deep understanding of their AWS environment, business objectives, technical architecture, and organizational dynamics. This continuity enables TAMs to provide context-aware guidance tailored to specific customer situations rather than generic recommendations. TAMs serve multiple critical functions in customer success: as trusted advisors providing strategic guidance on AWS service selection, architecture design, and cloud adoption strategies aligned with business goals; as proactive monitors conducting regular operational reviews identifying potential issues before they impact production, analyzing AWS Health Dashboard events, and recommending preventive measures; as coordinators facilitating connections between customers and AWS specialist teams including solutions architects, service teams, and AWS Professional Services when deep expertise is needed; as advocates representing customer interests within AWS, escalating critical issues, providing feedback to product teams, and ensuring customer concerns receive appropriate attention; as educators providing training on new AWS services, sharing best practices from across AWS customer base, and helping teams develop cloud skills; and as event planners helping customers prepare for high-stakes events like product launches, seasonal traffic spikes, migrations, or disaster recovery tests through pre-event planning, dry runs, and real-time support during events. The TAM relationship is highly consultative and collaborative. TAMs typically engage with customers through regular scheduled meetings including monthly or quarterly business reviews discussing AWS usage trends, cost optimization, upcoming initiatives, and strategic planning; workload-specific deep dives examining architecture, performance, security, and optimization opportunities for critical applications; operational reviews assessing AWS Health, support case trends, and proactive measures; and ad-hoc consultations addressing questions, concerns, or emerging requirements. TAMs leverage their extensive AWS knowledge, cross-customer experience, and internal AWS relationships to provide value beyond what customers could achieve independently. They understand AWS service roadmaps, emerging best practices, common pitfalls, and proven patterns, sharing these insights to help customers avoid problems and adopt innovations effectively. The proactive nature of TAM engagement distinguishes Enterprise Support—rather than waiting for customers to encounter problems and open support cases, TAMs actively monitor customer environments, identify opportunities, and reach out with recommendations. This proactive approach prevents issues, optimizes operations, and accelerates cloud maturity. TAM availability varies by customer region with TAMs providing support during business hours in customer time zones and establishing escalation procedures for after-hours critical issues. For global organizations, AWS can provide TAM coverage across multiple regions. The TAM also serves as customer advocate within AWS, escalating issues that require special attention, providing customer feedback to AWS service teams influencing product development, and ensuring customer success remains prioritized. Organizations maximizing TAM value engage actively with regular meetings, share business context and upcoming initiatives enabling proactive guidance, leverage TAM connections to specialist teams, and treat TAM as strategic partner rather than just support contact.

options.text: Support 24/7 through phone, chat, or email

explanation.summary: AWS Enterprise Support provides round-the-clock access to AWS Support engineers through multiple communication channels including phone, chat, and email, enabling customers to receive technical assistance anytime for production issues, architectural guidance, and operational questions.
keyPoints: 24/7/365 access to AWS Support engineers with no time restrictions or blackout periods
Multiple communication channels including phone for urgent issues, chat for real-time interaction, and email for detailed inquiries
Support available in multiple languages including English, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese
Unlimited support cases with no restrictions on quantity or frequency
Access to full AWS Support API enabling programmatic case management and automation
Priority routing to senior engineers for Enterprise Support customers
Support covers all AWS services including preview and beta services
examples: Production database outage at 3 AM Sunday triggers phone call to AWS Support receiving immediate assistance from senior DBA specialist
Developer uses chat during business hours for real-time troubleshooting of API Gateway configuration with support engineer
Architecture team submits detailed email inquiry about multi-region disaster recovery design receiving comprehensive written response with diagrams
Operations team opens support case via AWS Support Center web interface providing logs and screenshots for S3 performance investigation
Security incident at midnight triggers urgent phone support with AWS security specialist coordinating response
Development team uses AWS Support API to programmatically create cases from monitoring system when CloudWatch alarms trigger
explanation.additionalInfo: Round-the-clock support through multiple channels represents a fundamental capability of AWS Enterprise Support, ensuring customers can access technical assistance whenever issues arise regardless of time, day, or location. Unlike Developer Support with business hours email-only access or Business Support with 24/7 access only for urgent issues, Enterprise Support provides unrestricted 24/7 access through all channels for all severity levels. This comprehensive availability is critical for organizations running production workloads, operating globally across time zones, or requiring confidence that technical assistance is always available during incidents, deployments, or operational events. The multi-channel approach enables customers to select communication methods appropriate to their situations: phone support provides immediate voice communication ideal for urgent production issues requiring rapid coordination, complex troubleshooting benefiting from real-time discussion, or situations where speaking is more efficient than typing; chat support offers real-time text-based interaction suitable for moderate urgency issues, situations where customers want to multitask while receiving support, or when customers prefer written communication for documentation; email support allows detailed inquiries with attachments, screenshots, and logs where comprehensive written responses are valuable, or asynchronous communication convenient for non-urgent questions. AWS Support engineers staffing these channels are distributed globally ensuring native language support and coverage across time zones. The support team includes specialists with deep expertise in specific AWS services, architectural patterns, and technical domains. Enterprise Support customers benefit from priority routing to senior engineers with extensive experience, reducing time to resolution. Support cases can be submitted through multiple interfaces: AWS Support Center in the AWS Management Console providing web-based case creation with forms guiding information collection; AWS Support API enabling programmatic case management from custom tools, monitoring systems, or automation workflows; AWS Personal Health Dashboard showing AWS service events affecting customer resources with direct links to create support cases; and direct phone numbers for urgent voice access. The support experience is designed for enterprise operational needs with features including case management tracking case status, communications, and history; file attachments for sharing logs, configurations, and screenshots; severity levels from critical business-critical system down to general guidance determining response SLAs; case updates and notifications keeping customers informed of progress; and case history providing searchable archive of past issues and solutions. Support coverage extends across all AWS services including compute, storage, database, networking, analytics, machine learning, security, and hundreds of other services, as well as preview and beta services. Engineers assist with diverse needs: troubleshooting production issues and outages, architectural guidance and best practices, performance optimization and tuning, security configurations and compliance, cost optimization and resource rightsizing, AWS service questions and how-to guidance, and deployment and migration assistance. The 24/7 availability combined with multiple channels and unlimited cases enables customers to operate confidently knowing support is always accessible. Organizations leverage this capability for follow-the-sun operations where global teams hand off support as business hours shift across regions, incident response where problems may occur anytime requiring immediate assistance, major events like product launches or migrations where teams want support standing by, and routine operations where development and operations teams regularly consult support for guidance.

options.text: A dedicated consultant from the AWS Partner Network (APN)

explanation.summary: AWS Partner Network consultants are independent third-party providers separate from AWS Enterprise Support, offering implementation and managed services through partner relationships rather than being included features of support plans.
explanation.why: The AWS Partner Network consists of thousands of independent technology and consulting partners who provide services complementing AWS, including systems integrators implementing AWS solutions, managed service providers operating AWS environments, independent software vendors providing applications on AWS, and consulting partners offering strategic guidance. These partners are separate commercial entities from AWS with their own service offerings, pricing, and contracts. While AWS Enterprise Support includes a Technical Account Manager who is an AWS employee, it does not include dedicated consultants from APN partners. Customers engage APN partners through separate commercial relationships, selecting partners based on expertise, geography, industry focus, or specific needs. Some synergies exist between Enterprise Support and APN partners with TAMs sometimes recommending appropriate partners for customer needs, partners collaborating with AWS support on joint customer engagements, and customers using both TAM guidance and partner implementation services. However, APN partner consultants are not included in or provided by Enterprise Support subscription. Customers pay separately for partner services according to partner commercial terms. The distinction matters for budgeting and understanding what Enterprise Support provides versus what requires separate partner engagements.

options.text: A dedicated consultant from AWS Professional Services

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services is a separate paid consulting offering providing project-based expertise for migrations, modernization, and custom solutions, not included in Enterprise Support subscriptions which focus on ongoing operational support.
explanation.why: AWS Professional Services is a distinct business unit within AWS offering hands-on consulting and implementation services for specific projects. Professional Services consultants work on time-bounded engagements like cloud migrations, application modernization, data analytics implementations, machine learning projects, and custom solution development. These engagements are scoped, quoted, and billed separately from support plans with customers paying professional services fees based on consultant time and project scope. Enterprise Support, in contrast, provides ongoing operational support through TAMs and support engineers but does not include project-based consulting or implementation work. The TAM provides strategic guidance and operational support within the scope of the support subscription, while Professional Services consultants provide hands-on implementation work through separate paid engagements. Some coordination occurs between Enterprise Support TAMs and Professional Services with TAMs identifying customer needs that could benefit from Professional Services expertise, TAMs recommending Professional Services engagements for complex projects beyond TAM scope, and TAMs collaborating with Professional Services teams on joint customer initiatives. However, Professional Services consultants are not included in or provided by Enterprise Support. Customers must separately engage and pay for Professional Services if they need project-based consulting. The distinction is important for customers to understand what support provides versus when additional paid services are needed.

questions.question: Which Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources can customers use to support compliance for their applications? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: While AWS technical guides provide valuable implementation guidance, they are general technical documentation rather than compliance-specific resources designed to support audit and regulatory requirements.
explanation.why: AWS technical guides include service documentation, API references, user guides, getting started tutorials, and implementation examples focusing on technical functionality and operational procedures. These guides explain how AWS services work, how to configure them, and how to implement solutions, serving primarily technical audiences. While technical guides might mention security features or best practices that support compliance, they are not specifically designed as compliance resources. Compliance support requires specialized resources explaining regulatory frameworks, mapping AWS capabilities to compliance requirements, providing audit guidance, and offering compliance-specific implementation patterns. Technical guides might explain how to enable S3 encryption but not specifically address how encryption satisfies HIPAA requirements. The distinction matters because compliance teams need resources explicitly addressing regulatory obligations, audit procedures, and compliance frameworks rather than general technical documentation. AWS provides dedicated compliance resources through different channels including AWS Artifact for audit reports, compliance whitepapers for regulatory guidance, and AWS Auditor Learning Path for compliance education, making technical guides insufficient as primary compliance support resources.

explanation.summary: AWS advisories and bulletins communicate security vulnerabilities, service issues, and important announcements, serving as notification mechanisms rather than comprehensive compliance support resources.
explanation.why: AWS advisories and bulletins provide time-sensitive communications about security vulnerabilities affecting AWS services, service disruptions or degradations, important changes to services or APIs, deprecations and end-of-life notices, and emergency security patches. These communications are reactive notifications addressing specific events or issues requiring customer awareness and potential action. While security advisories are important for maintaining secure and compliant environments, they do not constitute comprehensive compliance support resources. Compliance requires ongoing resources like frameworks, audit reports, implementation guidance, training, and consultative support rather than event-driven notifications. Advisories might inform customers about vulnerabilities requiring patching to maintain compliance posture, but they don't provide the frameworks, audit evidence, or guidance necessary for achieving compliance. Customers need advisories as part of their security and compliance programs, but compliance support requires additional resources like AWS Artifact for audit reports, compliance whitepapers for implementation guidance, Auditor Learning Path for education, and account teams for consultative support. The question specifically asks about resources supporting compliance for applications, which requires proactive guidance and evidence rather than reactive notifications.

explanation.summary: AWS Auditor Learning Path is a specialized training program designed specifically for auditors, compliance professionals, and risk management teams, providing education on AWS security controls, compliance frameworks, audit methodologies, and how to assess AWS environments against regulatory requirements.
keyPoints: Specialized training curriculum designed for auditors, compliance officers, and risk management professionals
Covers AWS security controls, shared responsibility model, and compliance framework mappings
Provides guidance on auditing AWS environments and assessing compliance posture
Includes modules on specific regulations like HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, and SOC 2
Explains how to use AWS compliance resources including Artifact, Config, and Security Hub
Helps auditors understand AWS attestations, certifications, and third-party audit reports
Available through AWS Training and Certification platform at no cost
examples: External auditor completing Auditor Learning Path before conducting SOC 2 audit of customer AWS environment
Internal compliance team using Learning Path to understand how AWS services map to HIPAA requirements
Risk management professional taking courses to assess third-party vendor AWS usage
Financial services auditor learning how AWS Config can demonstrate compliance with regulatory controls
Healthcare compliance officer studying AWS HIPAA guidance to prepare for HHS audit
IT audit team completing Learning Path to develop AWS-specific audit procedures
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Auditor Learning Path represents AWS's purpose-built educational resource for compliance professionals, recognizing that auditors and compliance teams have specialized needs different from technical practitioners or business stakeholders. Traditional AWS training focuses on building and operating systems, but auditors need to understand how to evaluate AWS environments for compliance, interpret AWS audit reports, map AWS controls to regulatory requirements, and assess customer implementations. The Auditor Learning Path addresses these specific needs through curated curriculum covering fundamental topics, AWS-specific knowledge, and regulatory frameworks. The learning path includes multiple components: foundational courses explaining cloud computing concepts, AWS global infrastructure, and the shared responsibility model which is critical for understanding compliance boundaries; security and compliance courses detailing AWS security services like IAM, CloudTrail, Config, and Security Hub that auditors will examine during assessments; control frameworks courses mapping AWS capabilities to frameworks like NIST, ISO 27001, CIS, and regulatory requirements; service-specific compliance guidance explaining compliance considerations for services like EC2, S3, RDS, and Lambda; audit methodology courses providing approaches for auditing cloud environments including evidence collection, control testing, and documentation; and hands-on labs where auditors can practice evaluating AWS environments. The curriculum also addresses specific regulations: HIPAA courses explain HIPAA-eligible services, Business Associate Agreements, required safeguards, and auditing PHI protection; PCI DSS courses cover payment card environments, AWS's PCI compliance, and customer responsibilities; GDPR courses address data protection, privacy controls, and demonstrating GDPR compliance; FedRAMP courses guide government auditors through authorization processes; and SOC 2 courses explain trust principles and auditing service organizations. A key value of the Auditor Learning Path is teaching auditors how to leverage AWS-specific compliance resources: understanding AWS Artifact and how to access audit reports, interpreting third-party attestations and certifications, using AWS Config to assess resource compliance, leveraging Security Hub for compliance checks, and reviewing CloudTrail logs for audit evidence. The program helps auditors translate their traditional audit skills to cloud environments where infrastructure is abstracted, resources are ephemeral, and control implementation differs from on-premises environments. Auditors learn to ask appropriate questions during AWS audits, identify what evidence to collect, understand what AWS controls versus what customers control, and assess whether customer implementations meet regulatory requirements. The Learning Path is available through AWS Training and Certification platform at no cost, enabling widespread access for compliance professionals. Completion doesn't grant certification but provides knowledge necessary for conducting effective AWS audits. Organizations benefit when their auditors complete the Learning Path by ensuring audits are AWS-informed, reducing audit friction, enabling productive auditor interactions, and demonstrating commitment to compliance. Many organizations require external auditors to complete the Learning Path before beginning AWS audits to ensure auditors have baseline AWS knowledge.

explanation.summary: AWS account teams including solutions architects, customer success managers, and Technical Account Managers provide direct personalized guidance helping customers understand compliance requirements, design compliant architectures, implement appropriate controls, and navigate AWS compliance resources to meet regulatory obligations.
keyPoints: Provide personalized guidance tailored to customer's specific compliance requirements and industry regulations
Help customers understand shared responsibility model and which compliance controls they must implement
Assist with mapping AWS services and features to specific regulatory requirements like HIPAA, PCI DSS, or GDPR
Connect customers with AWS compliance specialists and resources including Artifact, whitepapers, and Partner solutions
Review customer architectures identifying compliance gaps and recommending improvements
Support customers preparing for audits by explaining AWS compliance posture and available evidence
Available through various support tiers with increasing engagement levels from Business to Enterprise Support
examples: Solutions architect helps healthcare customer design HIPAA-compliant architecture with appropriate encryption, access controls, and audit logging
TAM conducts compliance readiness review before customer's PCI DSS assessment, identifying gaps in network segmentation and logging
Account team connects financial services customer with AWS compliance specialists to understand FINRA requirements
Customer success manager guides retail customer through GDPR implementation including data residency, encryption, and privacy controls
Solutions architect provides compliance-focused architecture review mapping customer's design to SOC 2 trust principles
TAM coordinates with AWS legal team to answer customer questions about Business Associate Agreement for HIPAA workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS account teams represent one of the most valuable resources for compliance support, providing human expertise, personalized guidance, and direct access to AWS knowledge that complements technical documentation and self-service resources. Unlike generic documentation or automated tools, account teams understand customer-specific contexts including their industry, regulatory requirements, risk tolerance, existing infrastructure, and business constraints, enabling tailored compliance guidance. The composition and engagement level of account teams varies by AWS support tier: Developer Support provides limited account team access primarily through support cases; Business Support includes AWS Support engineers and some solutions architect engagement; Enterprise Support provides dedicated Technical Account Manager, priority access to solutions architects, and customer success managers creating comprehensive account team. These team members bring different expertise: solutions architects provide deep technical knowledge helping design compliant architectures, select appropriate AWS services, and implement security controls; Technical Account Managers offer strategic guidance, coordinate across AWS teams, and provide ongoing compliance advisement; customer success managers ensure customer achievement of business objectives including compliance goals; and support engineers assist with technical implementation and troubleshooting of compliance-related configurations. Account teams support compliance through multiple activities: architecture reviews where solutions architects evaluate customer designs against compliance frameworks identifying gaps, recommending AWS services that address requirements, suggesting architectural patterns proven for compliance, and documenting how the architecture meets specific regulatory controls; compliance planning where teams help customers understand which regulations apply, map AWS capabilities to regulatory requirements, identify customer responsibilities under shared responsibility model, and develop implementation roadmaps; implementation guidance where teams advise on configuring AWS services for compliance, enabling appropriate security features, implementing logging and monitoring, and establishing access controls; audit preparation where teams explain AWS compliance programs, demonstrate how to access audit reports through Artifact, review customer evidence collection approaches, and connect customers with AWS compliance specialists who can answer auditor questions; and problem solving where teams address compliance-specific challenges, unusual regulatory requirements, or complex multi-service compliance scenarios. A critical role account teams play is connecting customers with specialized AWS resources: referring customers to AWS Auditor Learning Path for auditor education, connecting with AWS compliance specialists for complex regulatory questions, facilitating introductions to AWS Partner Network compliance partners, providing access to AWS Professional Services for hands-on compliance implementations, and coordinating with AWS legal team for contract or Business Associate Agreement questions. Account teams also share cross-customer experience and best practices gained from working with numerous customers in similar industries, helping customers avoid common compliance pitfalls, learn from others' implementations, and adopt proven approaches. The consultative nature of account team engagement makes them particularly valuable for organizations new to AWS, undergoing compliance certifications, entering regulated industries, or facing complex compliance requirements. While documentation and training provide foundational knowledge, account teams apply that knowledge to specific customer situations, answer customer-specific questions, and guide implementation decisions. Organizations maximize value from account teams by engaging them early in compliance planning, sharing upcoming compliance initiatives and deadlines, asking specific questions rather than general requests, preparing for engagements with context about regulations and requirements, and maintaining ongoing relationships enabling teams to provide proactive guidance.

explanation.summary: AWS reference architecture diagrams provide technical blueprints and design patterns for building solutions on AWS, but they are general technical resources rather than compliance-specific support materials.
explanation.why: AWS reference architectures illustrate well-designed solutions for common use cases like web applications, data analytics, IoT, machine learning, and microservices. These diagrams show how AWS services connect, data flows, component relationships, and architectural patterns following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles. While reference architectures might incorporate security best practices and mention compliance considerations, they are primarily technical design documents rather than compliance support resources. Compliance support requires regulatory guidance, audit frameworks, control mappings, and implementation specifics for meeting legal requirements, which reference architectures don't typically provide. A reference architecture might show a multi-tier web application with load balancers, application servers, and databases, explaining technical design but not specifically addressing how this architecture satisfies HIPAA, PCI DSS, or GDPR requirements. Customers might use reference architectures as starting points for compliant solutions, but would need additional compliance-specific resources like AWS compliance whitepapers, Auditor Learning Path, and account team guidance to ensure regulatory requirements are met. The question asks specifically about resources supporting compliance, not general architectural guidance, making reference architectures insufficient as primary compliance resources.

questions.question: A security engineer discovered a vulnerability in an Amazon Web Services (AWS) service. Where should this engineer report their findings?

explanation.summary: AWS advisories and bulletins serve as the official channel for AWS to communicate security vulnerabilities and for customers to report discovered vulnerabilities in AWS services, with AWS Security team monitoring these channels and coordinating vulnerability disclosure and remediation.
keyPoints: Official AWS channel for security vulnerability reporting and disclosure
AWS Security team monitors submissions and coordinates vulnerability response
Used for reporting vulnerabilities in AWS services, infrastructure, or websites
Follows responsible disclosure practices protecting customers while vulnerabilities are addressed
AWS publishes bulletins notifying customers of vulnerabilities and available mitigations
Part of AWS Vulnerability Reporting Program encouraging security research
Alternative reporting via aws-security@amazon.com email address
examples: Security researcher discovers authentication bypass in AWS service and reports through AWS Vulnerability Reporting page
Engineer identifies potential data exposure in AWS console and submits report to aws-security@amazon.com
External penetration tester finds privilege escalation vulnerability in AWS API and reports through official channels
Customer security team discovers configuration issue in AWS service that could affect other customers and reports to AWS Security
Bug bounty researcher identifies cross-site scripting vulnerability in AWS website and submits through responsible disclosure program
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS advisories and bulletins represent the official communication channel between AWS and the security community for vulnerability disclosure, coordinating between vulnerability discovery, AWS remediation, and customer notification. When security engineers, researchers, or customers discover potential vulnerabilities in AWS services, infrastructure, websites, or applications, AWS needs to be notified through proper channels to enable responsible disclosure rather than public disclosure that could enable exploitation before fixes are available. AWS maintains a formal Vulnerability Reporting Program defining how individuals should report security findings. The program encourages security researchers, customers, and ethical hackers to report vulnerabilities they discover through responsible disclosure, meaning reporting privately to AWS rather than publicly disclosing, allowing AWS reasonable time to investigate and remediate before public disclosure, and following testing guidelines that avoid impacting other customers. The primary reporting channels are: AWS Vulnerability Reporting web form on the AWS Security Center website providing structured submission process; aws-security@amazon.com email address for direct communication with AWS Security team; and AWS Bug Bounty Program for eligible vulnerabilities offering financial rewards. When vulnerabilities are reported, AWS Security team follows defined processes: acknowledging receipt of reports typically within 72 hours; investigating reported vulnerabilities to confirm existence, assess severity, and determine scope; developing and testing fixes or mitigations; deploying remediation across AWS infrastructure; and publishing security bulletins notifying customers of vulnerabilities and available protections. AWS Security Bulletins published after remediation provide information about the vulnerability, affected services or components, severity rating, timeline of discovery and remediation, and customer actions if any are required. The bulletins use responsible disclosure practices, providing enough information for customers to understand risks and take protective actions while not providing exploit details that could enable attacks. The advisory and bulletin system serves multiple purposes: enabling AWS to learn about vulnerabilities from external sources leveraging community security expertise; coordinating remediation before vulnerabilities are publicly known or exploited; communicating with customers about security issues affecting their AWS usage; demonstrating AWS commitment to security and transparency; and maintaining trust through responsible vulnerability handling. AWS distinguishes between vulnerabilities in AWS services requiring AWS remediation versus misconfigurations in customer environments requiring customer action. When reported vulnerabilities involve customer configuration issues rather than AWS service flaws, AWS may provide guidance to the reporting party while not issuing bulletins since the issue doesn't affect AWS services generally. The system also covers vulnerabilities in AWS-developed open source software, AWS-operated websites and services, and AWS physical infrastructure when applicable. Best practices for reporting vulnerabilities include providing detailed description of the issue, steps to reproduce, affected AWS services or endpoints, potential impact assessment, and any proof-of-concept code, while avoiding testing that would affect other AWS customers, cause service disruptions, or involve unauthorized access to customer data.

explanation.summary: Amazon Cognito is an identity and access management service for applications, not a security vulnerability reporting channel, making it completely inappropriate for reporting AWS service vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: Amazon Cognito provides user authentication, authorization, and user management for web and mobile applications. The service enables developers to add sign-up and sign-in functionality, integrate with social identity providers, implement multi-factor authentication, and manage user pools. Cognito is an AWS service for building applications, not a communication channel or security reporting mechanism. Attempting to report AWS service vulnerabilities through Cognito makes no sense as Cognito provides no mechanism for submitting security reports, the service has no connection to AWS Security team vulnerability intake processes, and using an application service for security reporting would be ineffective and inappropriate. The confusion might arise from Cognito being a security-related service dealing with authentication, but service functionality is completely different from vulnerability reporting channels. Reporting vulnerabilities requires dedicated communication channels monitored by security teams, not using random AWS services. AWS provides specific channels for vulnerability reporting including AWS Security Center web form, aws-security@amazon.com email, and AWS Security Bulletins, none of which involve Cognito. The inclusion of Cognito as an option tests whether candidates understand the difference between AWS services and AWS support/security communication channels.

explanation.summary: AWS DevOps and Automation toolkit refers to services and tools for software delivery and infrastructure automation, not vulnerability reporting channels, making it inappropriate for reporting security findings.
explanation.why: AWS DevOps and Automation toolkit is a collective term for services and tools supporting continuous integration/continuous deployment, infrastructure as code, and automation including AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodeCommit, CloudFormation, Systems Manager, and related services. These tools enable automated software delivery, infrastructure provisioning, configuration management, and operational automation. While DevOps practices include security considerations and may incorporate security testing in CI/CD pipelines, the DevOps toolkit is not a communication or reporting channel for vulnerability disclosure. Attempting to report AWS service vulnerabilities through DevOps tools would be ineffective as these services provide automation capabilities not communication mechanisms, have no connection to AWS Security team vulnerability response, and are designed for building and deploying applications not for security reporting. The confusion might arise from DevSecOps concepts integrating security into DevOps practices, but this refers to incorporating security testing and controls in development workflows, not using DevOps tools as vulnerability reporting channels. Proper vulnerability reporting requires dedicated security channels including AWS Vulnerability Reporting web form, aws-security@amazon.com email, and AWS Security Bulletins where AWS Security team monitors submissions and coordinates response. The question tests understanding of appropriate channels for security-critical communications.

explanation.summary: AWS helpdesk or support cases are appropriate for customer-specific technical issues but not the designated channel for reporting security vulnerabilities in AWS services requiring coordinated disclosure and security team response.
explanation.why: AWS Support provides technical assistance for customer AWS usage through support cases addressing service issues, configuration questions, troubleshooting, and guidance. Support cases are appropriate for customer-specific problems like instance connectivity issues, service configuration assistance, or account questions. However, security vulnerabilities affecting AWS services generally require different handling than typical support cases because vulnerabilities impact all AWS customers not just the reporting party, require coordination between AWS Security team and service teams, involve responsible disclosure practices limiting vulnerability details before remediation, and may require security bulletins notifying all customers. While support cases might eventually route security reports to appropriate teams, the designated channels for vulnerability reporting are AWS Security Center vulnerability reporting page and aws-security@amazon.com email monitored by AWS Security team. Using general support helpdesk for vulnerability reporting could delay response, risk inappropriate disclosure, or result in reports being handled as routine technical cases rather than security issues requiring specialized response. AWS maintains separate security channels specifically for vulnerability disclosure ensuring reports reach security specialists, follow responsible disclosure practices, and receive appropriate priority. Organizations and individuals discovering AWS service vulnerabilities should use official security reporting channels rather than general support to ensure proper handling.

questions.question: Which statement describes the service that Amazon Web Services (AWS) account teams provide?

options.text: They provide customers with compliance reports of their applications

explanation.summary: AWS account teams do not audit or provide compliance reports for customer applications, as this would require assessing customer-controlled workloads which falls outside the scope of AWS account team services.
explanation.why: Compliance reporting for applications requires independent third-party auditors to assess whether customer implementations meet regulatory requirements. AWS account teams including solutions architects, TAMs, and customer success managers provide guidance, architecture reviews, and recommendations, but they do not perform compliance audits or issue compliance reports certifying customer applications. Compliance assessments must be independent and objective, performed by qualified auditors without conflicts of interest. AWS account teams work collaboratively with customers as trusted advisors, which creates conflicts incompatible with independent audit roles. Additionally, customer applications and their compliance are customer responsibilities under the shared responsibility model, with AWS providing compliant infrastructure and guidance but not assessing or certifying customer workloads. AWS account teams can help customers prepare for audits by reviewing architectures, identifying potential gaps, and recommending improvements, and can explain AWS infrastructure compliance through Artifact reports, but they do not assess or report on customer application compliance. Customers obtain compliance reports by engaging independent auditing firms who assess customer environments and issue reports like SOC 2, ISO certifications, or regulatory compliance attestations specific to customer implementations.

options.text: They guide customers through deployment and implementation

explanation.summary: AWS account teams including solutions architects, Technical Account Managers, and customer success managers provide strategic and technical guidance helping customers plan, design, deploy, and implement AWS solutions effectively, offering expertise on architecture, best practices, service selection, and operational excellence.
keyPoints: Provide architecture guidance and design reviews ensuring solutions follow AWS best practices
Help customers select appropriate AWS services for their specific requirements and use cases
Offer implementation roadmaps and phased deployment strategies for complex solutions
Share best practices and lessons learned from across AWS customer base
Coordinate with AWS specialist teams when deep expertise in specific domains is needed
Support major initiatives including migrations, modernizations, and new product launches
Available at different engagement levels based on AWS support tier
examples: Solutions architect helps customer design three-tier web application architecture with Auto Scaling, load balancing, and RDS Multi-AZ
TAM guides customer through migration of on-premises datacenter to AWS including assessment, planning, and execution phases
Account team assists customer implementing microservices architecture with containers, API Gateway, and Lambda
Solutions architect provides Well-Architected review identifying improvements in security, reliability, and cost optimization
TAM helps customer prepare for major product launch including load testing, capacity planning, and monitoring setup
Customer success manager works with customer to establish AWS landing zone with multi-account structure and governance
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS account teams serve as trusted advisors and strategic partners helping customers successfully adopt AWS, design effective solutions, implement best practices, and achieve business objectives through cloud technology. The core value account teams provide is guidance through the complexity of cloud adoption, translating business requirements into technical implementations, and accelerating customer success by sharing AWS expertise and proven patterns. Account team composition and engagement intensity varies by support tier with Business Support providing access to solutions architects for architecture guidance and troubleshooting, and Enterprise Support including dedicated Technical Account Manager plus priority access to solutions architects and customer success managers for comprehensive account management. These team members bring complementary capabilities with solutions architects providing deep technical expertise in AWS services, architectural patterns, and implementation approaches, Technical Account Managers offering strategic guidance, proactive account management, and coordination across AWS resources, and customer success managers ensuring customers achieve business outcomes and fully leverage AWS capabilities. The guidance account teams provide spans the entire customer journey from initial AWS adoption through ongoing optimization. During planning and design phases, teams help customers understand AWS service options, evaluate architectural approaches, design solutions meeting functional and non-functional requirements, plan for scalability and resilience, estimate costs, and develop implementation roadmaps. During deployment phases, teams provide implementation guidance on service configurations, networking design, security controls, monitoring and logging, automation approaches, and integration patterns. Post-deployment, teams support operational excellence through architecture reviews identifying optimization opportunities, performance tuning recommendations, cost optimization guidance, security enhancements, and preparation for business events like product launches or seasonal traffic. Account teams excel at providing context-aware guidance understanding customer industries, regulatory requirements, technical constraints, organizational dynamics, and business goals, enabling recommendations tailored to specific customer situations rather than generic advice. The guidance is consultative with account teams working collaboratively with customer technical teams, asking questions to understand requirements and constraints, offering multiple approaches with trade-off analysis, and empowering customer decision-making rather than prescribing solutions. When customer needs exceed account team expertise, teams coordinate access to AWS specialists including service team experts, AWS Professional Services consultants, security specialists, cost optimization experts, and AWS Partner Network partners, facilitating connections and ensuring customers receive comprehensive support.

options.text: They provide customer support for deployed applications

explanation.summary: AWS account teams focus on strategic guidance and architecture rather than ongoing application support, which is provided through AWS Support engineers via support cases for technical troubleshooting and issue resolution.
explanation.why: There is an important distinction between strategic guidance from account teams and operational support from support engineers. AWS account teams including solutions architects, TAMs, and customer success managers provide proactive strategic guidance, architecture reviews, planning assistance, and long-term relationship management, operating at a consultative level focused on design, optimization, and strategic initiatives. In contrast, AWS Support engineers provide reactive technical support through support cases, troubleshooting specific issues, diagnosing service problems, resolving technical incidents, and answering technical how-to questions about AWS services. When customers encounter production issues, have questions about service behavior, or need help troubleshooting problems, they open support cases handled by support engineers who specialize in technical problem resolution. Account teams may be involved in major incidents through TAM escalation or coordination roles, and may proactively identify issues during account reviews, but they do not provide day-to-day application support or troubleshoot individual technical issues. The roles are complementary with support engineers handling tactical technical support issues while account teams provide strategic guidance and planning. Customers with Enterprise Support benefit from both dedicated TAM strategic guidance and unlimited access to support engineers for technical troubleshooting, but these remain distinct services with different purposes and engagement models.

options.text: They perform security tests on customer applications, such as penetration testing

explanation.summary: AWS account teams do not perform penetration testing or security assessments of customer applications, as security testing is either performed by customers themselves, third-party security firms, or through separate AWS services like Inspector.
explanation.why: Penetration testing involves actively attempting to exploit vulnerabilities in systems to assess security posture, requiring specialized security testing skills, tools, and methodologies. AWS account teams including solutions architects and TAMs are not penetration testers and do not perform security testing of customer applications. Under the shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for security of their applications and can perform their own security testing or engage third-party security testing firms. AWS provides services that enable security testing including Amazon Inspector for automated vulnerability scanning, AWS Security Hub for security findings aggregation, and policies allowing customers to perform penetration testing on their own AWS resources with notification requirements for certain testing types. Account teams can provide guidance on security architecture, recommend security best practices, review security configurations, and advise on security testing approaches, but they do not execute penetration tests. If customers need hands-on security testing beyond self-service tools, they engage specialized AWS Professional Services security consultants or third-party security firms who provide penetration testing services, but these are separate paid engagements not included in account team services. The distinction matters because penetration testing requires specific expertise, liability considerations, and formal scoping separate from advisory guidance that account teams provide.
